title: Mesh-independent structured observation grids
summary: Samples serial or distributed FEM fields on stable Cartesian coordinates and exports explicit axes, array layout, units, components, and optional geometry masks for external neural-operator and digital-twin workflows.

science.statement: A fixed physical observation operator separates the mesh used to solve each FEM case from the tensor coordinates consumed by a learned operator or compared with sensors.

equations.label: observation operator
equations.description: The same ordered physical coordinates are evaluated for every simulation and MPI partition.

equations.label: coordinate registration
equations.description: A reviewed affine map records axis orientation, scale, and origin between observation and model coordinates.

equations.label: operator-learning map
equations.description: Input and output fields require explicit discretization, coordinate, component, and boundary encodings.

inputs.name: observation grid
inputs.type: one to three strictly increasing Cartesian axes
inputs.description: Defines shape, order, coordinate system, and stable point identities.

inputs.name: finite-element field
inputs.type: scalar, vector, or tensor DOLFINx Function
inputs.description: May be distributed; ownership is resolved collectively.

inputs.name: optional affine coordinate map
inputs.type: invertible one-, two-, or three-dimensional matrix and offset
inputs.unit_role: explicit source and target coordinate units
inputs.description: Maps publication, sensor, or laboratory coordinates to model sampling coordinates.

outputs.name: FEMFieldSample
outputs.type: coordinates, structured values, scientific FieldEncoding, metadata, and optional mask
outputs.description: Portable NPZ or optional PyTorch tensors without prescribing a network architecture.

outputs.name: RectilinearObservation
outputs.type: two physical axes, image-layout scalar values, mask, units, and configuration
outputs.description: Provides an unambiguous publication/experiment comparison layout and dependency-free NPZ exchange.

assumptions: Every case uses the same declared observation grid when samples are combined.
Coordinates and physical units are consistent across the campaign.
Outside-geometry values use an explicit mask rather than being mistaken for physical zeros.
conventions: Stored values use grid axes followed by field-component axes.
C array order is the default and is recorded.
A true mask entry denotes a point inside the finite-element mesh.
FEMFieldSample stores observation coordinates and, when registered, the distinct model sampling coordinates.
applicability: FNO-style structured-grid datasets, sensor-aligned digital-twin data, field comparison, and mesh-family campaigns.
limitations: Graph and reduced-basis encodings are not yet executable.
No production neural-operator trainer is bundled.
Coordinate registration is currently affine; non-affine optical calibration needs an external reviewed transform.
Online sensor ingestion, assimilation, and uncertainty updating remain external future services.

usage.minimal_example: grid = surrogates.regular_grid(bounds=((0,L),(0,H)), shape=(128,64)); registration = surrogates.AffineCoordinateMap(matrix=A, offset=b); sample = datasets.fem_observation_sample(U, grid, unit='m', outside='mask', coordinate_map=registration); image = datasets.RectilinearObservation.from_field_sample(sample)

validation_rules: Reject non-monotone axes, inconsistent bounds/shapes, and unknown outside policies.
Compare analytical affine fields on serial and two-rank meshes.
Preserve the same value bytes on every MPI rank.
Round-trip mapped sampling coordinates and explicit rectilinear layout.

references.title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
NIST human-centered framework to update digital twins
